title: Musical family and buying an alto horn
summary: Parker's father, brother and brother-in-law were musicians; he tells of seeing an alto sax at a shop, and where they lived.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did you have any musicians in your family?

My daddy, sure. That's how we love him. But when the professor, Professor Hinger, white man, would be teaching, I'd be at that winter. I'd be at that winter and let everything he tell my daddy do. My daddy was a musician, my brother, my brother-in-law. All of them, all in one house. All of them was in the same house. My brother-in-law played the bass, bass violin, you know? My brother, he played the bass, tuba. My brother played the tuba. My daddy was a drummer. My dear I remember the name, yeah. But anyhow, they had a 16-piece brass band. Then all the drummers went off, some guy. We used to put little Willie on the drum, out of me. We used to play the drum out of the street, you know, Ken. Every night we'd be out there, field band. Oh, they put me on the drum. And that's why I stayed.
Did you have them play any other instruments?
Other instruments? Yes. Alto, sure. French horn, clarinet.
That was an alto horn or an alto sax?

Alto horn. I could've been a good alto sax player, but I didn't know. I went uptown to get some reeds from the tag at Grunewald, you know? I used to go up there and get a dollar with a reed at once. And when I come out, I seen horn, seen alto sax in the show cave. So I called. I said, Mr. Hennig, come here. How much you want for this pipe horn right in the door? What's a pipe horn? I said, come here and let me show you. He said, that's the alto sax. I let you have it for $60. What section of the city did you live in? I said, I'm going to go up there. I'm going to go up there. I'm going to go up there. I'm going to go up there. What section of the city did you live in?
What section of the city did you live in?
When we were young. Right down there. Right down Bourbon and Marie. Bourbon and Marie. Bourbon and Marie right down there.
